In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a single bout of moderate intensity exercise decreases postprandial lipid concentrations but does not affect changes to PBMC HMGCOA reductase, VLDL or low density lipoproteins receptor mRNA expression.

exercise-induced energy deficits are associated with a decrease in postprandal TG concentrations but that this decrease is independent of changes in PBMC expression of genes related to lipoprotein metabolism and that energy replacement does not affect postprandial lipid concentrations.

energy replacement with glucose does not affect postprandial lipid metabolism after exercise and exercise itself does not affect changes to PBMC mRNA expression of genes involved in lipoprotein metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
moderate intensity aerobic exercise decreases postprandial lipidemia and this effect is not influenced by the energy deficit induced by exercise.
a single bout of moderate intensity aerobic exercise can reduce postprandial lipidemia and that energy replacement by glucose does not alter this reduction.

a single bout of exercise with or without energy replacement can decrease postprandanial lipemia but the underlying mechanism is not related to changes in the PBMC mRNA expression of VLDL and/or LDL receptors or HMGCR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
energy replacement by glucose does not affect postprandial lipid metabolism after moderate intensity exercise in healthy men.
exercise-induced energy deficits are not required to reduce postprandial lipid concentrations.
exercise can decrease post-prandial TG concentrations independent of energy replacement.
